$comment: RFC 0263 §B — red runs that show a cited conformance leg can fail. One row per sabotage: the requirement id, the scenario, one sentence naming what was broken, the subject it ran on ({host, build}; never a certified committed bundle — that recorded the pass), the suite version, result executed-fail, and the date. witnessSha256 is optional (the red bundle's digest, when one was cut). Checked by scripts/check-accepted-predicate.mjs rules 5 and 6 and scripts/check-sabotage-ledger.mjs (scripts/lib/sabotage-ledger.mjs). From RFC 0260, an RFC goes Accepted only when every id its Falsifiability table names on a witnessable row has a row here. Older RFCs are not retroactively invalidated; a backfill is invited (RFCS/registers/0263-sabotage-ledger.gaps.md).

derive-core-adoption.mjs stopped requiring a review row for a family whose derived adoption is none, so a missing row passed.
derive-core-adoption.mjs stopped comparing a keep row with the baseline, so a renewal that changed only reviewBy passed.
derive-core-adoption.mjs stopped refusing a keep row whose reviewBy is below the release minor, so an overdue review passed.

rows.sabotage: The replay family's normativeText was removed from the committed declaration, so one family was undeclared against a baseline of zero.
The cap was computed as 25,000 + 200 x (homed - 9 + 1), one family's words more than the homed families earn.
The end-of-support verdict left undeclared families out of the fatal list, so a family with no home was no longer named as uncovered.
V1Carried was set to [replay], a family that is not v1-dependent, so it no longer equalled the computed v1-dependent set.
Clause (b) was disabled, so an anchor outside the schema's closed enum no longer refused the list.
witnessDigest left host.deployment out of the preimage, so a companion's marker no longer changed its signed digest.
A paired companion counted every executed-pass row, not only the rows on the harness-trust-anchor list.
Same-image compared only that both builds were image digests, not that the two digests were equal.
An attestation that did not verify under the named published key no longer blocked pairing.
Equivalent-discovery checked only that both documents existed, not that their normalized forms were equal.
isCompanion dropped the legacy unmarked-companion digests, so the committed 2026-09-25 companion was read as a served host.
The v1 section schema's locale patterns were restored to RFC 0103's ^[a-z]{2}(-[A-Z]{2})?$, so extended BCP 47 keys such as zh-Hant-TW no longer validated there.
The v2 section schema's locale patterns were made case-insensitive, so non-canonical tags such as EN, en-us and zh-hans validated.
The putContentSection body's locale pattern in api/openapi.yaml was left on RFC 0103's grammar while the schemas carried the new one.
The v2 section schema's locale patterns required a three-letter language, so two-letter keys the RFC 0103 grammar admitted no longer validated.
resolveSection skipped the language-script step, so zh-Hant-TW on {zh-Hant, zh} overlaid zh instead of zh-Hant.
resolveSection tried any two-subtag prefix, not only a four-letter script subtag, so de-CH-1996 resolved differently from RFC 0103.
part.schema.json gained a filename2 property that a2a.proto v1.0.1's Part message does not declare.
Both v2 turn defs dropped minItems from parts, so an empty parts array validated.
The ConversationTurn def in conversation-event.schema.json gained maxItems 64 on parts, so the two turn defs' parts subschemas were no longer deep-equal.
The exportFormats item pattern lost its media-type branch, so lowercase media types such as application/pdf no longer validated.
